bands.title: Bracing for the worst
bands.summary: Your answers suggest the future feels uncertain and setbacks hit hard right now. That is understandable, and outlook can change.

bands.title: Cautious outlook
bands.summary: Your answers suggest you tend to expect difficulties, though you can sometimes see the bright side.

bands.title: Hopeful and steady
bands.summary: Your answers suggest you generally expect things to work out and can recover from setbacks.

bands.title: Strongly optimistic
bands.summary: Your answers suggest a hopeful outlook and a strong ability to bounce back.

support.text: If you have been feeling low or hopeless for a while, it can really help to talk to someone you trust or a professional. You can also try the Low Mood check-in in MindCheck.

outlook.low: The future can look uncertain or difficult to you right now.
outlook.moderate: You hope things will work out, with some reservations.
outlook.high: You tend to expect good things from the future.
outlook.reflect: What is one thing you are looking forward to?
outlook.tip: Each evening, write down one thing that went better than expected.

steadiness.low: Your mood seems to dip often at the moment.
steadiness.moderate: Your mood is fairly steady, with some low days.
steadiness.high: You usually feel settled and comfortable in yourself.
steadiness.reflect: What lifts your mood most reliably?
steadiness.tip: Plan one small, enjoyable activity into each day, even on busy days.

bounce_back.low: Setbacks seem to stay with you for a while.
bounce_back.moderate: You usually recover from setbacks, given some time.
bounce_back.high: You tend to recover quickly and keep going after setbacks.
bounce_back.reflect: Think of a past setback you got through. What helped?
bounce_back.tip: After a setback, ask: "What can I learn here, and what is my next small step?"

coping.low: Calming down, adapting or asking for help can feel hard right now.
coping.moderate: You have some ways of coping, though they don't always work.
coping.high: You have good ways to calm yourself, adapt and get support.
coping.reflect: Who could you lean on when things get hard?
coping.tip: Write a short list of things that calm you, and keep it on your phone for tough moments.

suggestions: Optimism is not ignoring problems. It is expecting that you can find a way through them.
Resilience grows through support, rest and small wins, not by pushing through alone.
A rough month can lower this score. Retake it after a while to see how it changes.
note: Your score is the average of all 20 answers, shown on a 0–100 scale. Questions 1–10 are the public-domain IPIP Optimism scale; questions 11–20 were written for MindCheck. The combined score is not validated and does not assess any condition.
